You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failure test 'testLinearCombinationWithSingleElementArray' creates two arrays with a single element and calls MathArrays.linearCombination. The expected result is the product of the single elements.

Looking at MathArrays.linearCombination(double[], double[]):
- Line 816 gets the length of the input arrays.
- Lines 817-819 check if the lengths differ and throw an exception if so.
- Lines 823-842 fill prodHigh[] with each element-wise product and calculate prodLowSum as a correction.
- Lines 845-849 try to create a summation of the elements of prodHigh[], using prodHigh[0] and prodHigh[1].
- Here, an index access prodHigh[1] occurs without checking if the input length > 1.

The test with length 1 causes this access to prodHigh[1] to throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.

The current bug report explicitly points out this problem with the line:
double prodHighNext = prodHigh[1];

It states that linearCombination should check length == 1 and if so, fall back to simple multiplication. That is not done in the current code.

Thus, the root cause is that the code assumes input array length is at least 2 starting at line 846, but does not check. It should have a separate path for length == 1 to simply return a[0] * b[0] or handle array indexing safely.

The loop starting at line 852 also assumes length > 2 since it loops up to len - 1.

In conclusion, the fault is that MathArrays.linearCombination does not handle the case where input arrays have length 1, causing an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException when accessing prodHigh[1]. This matches the observed failure and the report. The fix should add a length==1 check and return the product directly in that case, preventing the invalid access.

Recent bug reports are unrelated.

Summary:
- The test fails with ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException due to indexing prodHigh[1] when input length is 1.
- The code assumes length >= 2 during summation steps without checking.
- The bug report correctly identifies this and requests a fallback for length==1.
- The bug is here in MathArrays.linearCombination, lines ~845-850.

This is the detailed step-by-step diagnosis.
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test 'testLinearCombinationWithSingleElementArray' exercises MathArrays.linearCombination with single-element arrays. Inspecting the linearCombination method reveals that after computing element-wise products into the prodHigh array, the code attempts to access prodHigh[1] without checking that the array length is greater than 1. Since the input length is exactly 1, this results in an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. The current bug report pinpoints this exact line and suggests falling back to simple multiplication when the array length is 1. Thus, the bug arises because the method assumes input arrays have length at least 2 for the summation logic, but does not handle length == 1 as a special case. This mismatch leads to the exception seen in the test. Therefore, the fault lies in MathArrays.linearCombination lacking a length==1 conditional handling that returns the simple product directly and prevents out-of-bounds array access. The recent bug reports are unrelated. This diagnosis matches the symptoms and source code behavior exactly.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
